title: Insulin Pump Users and the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program
content:
Holding an insulin pump program decides which benefit pays for pump insulin under the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program.

## Benefit rules

**Opening the Part B program.** The Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program is opened only for a customer who holds a pump program on the Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program tier in active or on hold status, because Medicare Part B pays for insulin used in a durable insulin pump it covers. Whether the customer holds such a pump program, and its status, is read from the customer's Insulin Pump Program records.

**Pump insulin stays on Part B.** For such a customer, insulin used in the pump is never dispensed on the Part D tier: a rapid-acting vial the prescription directs for the pump is dispensed only as J1817 on the Part B pump insulin program, while backup pens or vials for injection remain on the Part D program.

**When the pump program closes.** When the pump program closes, the Part B pump insulin program receives no further refills and the customer's insulin moves to their Part D program on a new prescription.

## Points of judgement

| Customer's Insulin Pump Program | Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program may be opened? |
|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program tier, active | Yes |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program tier, on hold | Yes |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program tier, closed | No |
| Pump program on any other Insulin Pump tier | No |
| No pump program | No |

- *Where does a rapid-acting vial for the pump go for a customer holding the Original Medicare pump program?* It is dispensed only as J1817 on the Part B pump insulin program; backup pens or vials for injection remain on the Part D program.
- *What happens to the Part B pump insulin program after the pump program closes?* It receives no further refills, and the customer's insulin moves to their Part D program on a new prescription.
